assessments.title: [mt-context 16/21] Propagate the caller's tenant to the AI gateway and attribute every call
assessments.rationale: Tenant identity crosses several clients and the AI gateway, with authentication ordering and atomic reservation rejection.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 05/23] Record module data migrations per tenant
assessments.rationale: Advisory locking and migration conflicts change scope; concurrency and repeated execution need explicit proof.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 06/23] Run the post-migration cutover steps per tenant or retire them
assessments.rationale: Existing tenant iteration and cutover mechanisms are composed with bounded pool cleanup and isolated failures.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 07/23] Deduplicate and store blobs per tenant
assessments.rationale: Tenant deduplication combines database constraints, filesystem keys and concurrent writes across several services.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 08/23] Authorize blob downloads in scope before the conditional branch
assessments.rationale: A bounded authorization transaction moves before conditional HTTP branches while existing streaming remains intact.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 16/23] Validate stored item and database references inside the tenant
assessments.rationale: Existing lookups and write transactions enforce defined reference checks, ordering and indistinguishable errors.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 17/23] Address tenant events and agent runs to the tenant's user
assessments.rationale: Recipient ownership changes across production paths and 56 declared Touches entries, creating substantial omission risk.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 18/23] Send operator alerts to every admin without tenant content
assessments.rationale: Cross-tenant admin delivery combines deduplication and rollback of the complete change on recipient failure.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 19/23] Remove the earliest-user lookups
assessments.rationale: Defined helper removal and tenant backfill follow existing patterns and need database integration proof.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 22/23] Prune the remaining id-only item lookups to the tenant's partitions
assessments.rationale: Several existing queries are narrowed to tenant partitions, with query-plan and RLS result assertions.

assessments.title: [mt-scope 23/23] Revoke a user's push registrations on password reset
assessments.rationale: One targeted revocation shares the password-reset transaction and uses established store patterns.

assessments.title: [mt-realtime 01/04] Stamp the tenant on every NOTIFY and deliver only to that tenant's sockets
assessments.rationale: A new tenant envelope crosses NOTIFY, sockets, listeners and transaction scopes.

assessments.title: [mt-realtime 02/04] Authorize doc sync inside the socket's tenant
assessments.rationale: CRDT subscription isolation and asynchronous document authorization require careful handoff and fan-out.

assessments.title: [mt-realtime 03/04] Authorize agent-run watching by tenant visibility
assessments.rationale: Defined tenant guards extend an existing watcher and need replay handoff integration coverage.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 01/08] Let only the run's owner decide its approval requests
assessments.rationale: A bounded ownership predicate extends existing reads and UPDATE paths with atomic decision tests.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 02/08] Validate MCP server connection configs on every write path
assessments.rationale: Existing schemas and hooks gain precisely specified MCP validation guards.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 03/08] Confine the stdio transport to a human writer in an admin's tenant
assessments.rationale: A new human-writer provenance contract authorizes host stdio commands across several layers.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 04/08] Re-check the transport at spawn and give stdio children an allowlisted environment
assessments.rationale: Exact environment allow-lists and spawn-time guards apply the previously defined stdio contract.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 05/08] Check resolved outbound addresses at connect time for MCP and web push
assessments.rationale: DNS rebinding protection, address classification and connect-time enforcement introduce a network mechanism across two transports.

assessments.title: [mt-ai-budgets 02/04] Enforce per-tenant caps and a global safety cap under the existing reservation lock
assessments.rationale: Global and tenant budgets share reservation locking, SQL routing, startup settings and multiple endpoints.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 03/10] Create item partitions without an exclusive lock on items
assessments.rationale: Postgres partition DDL changes lock behavior and must preserve catalog equivalence, RLS and grants.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 01/12] Gate admin routes behind the admin role and audit every admin action
assessments.rationale: Admin route gates, system scopes and atomic audit writes establish a cross-cutting authorization contract.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 02/12] Add admin operations health from content-free aggregates
assessments.rationale: One defined aggregate definer function and health report use the preceding admin route mechanism.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 03/12] Let admins set per-tenant AI caps and see per-tenant spend
assessments.rationale: Defined budget endpoints and SQL aggregates use existing admin gates and audit transactions.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 04/12] Let admins create, list and revoke invitations
assessments.rationale: An invitation lifecycle combines tokens, transactions, expiry and post-commit SMTP delivery.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 05/12] Let admins suspend, reactivate and change roles with a last-admin guard
assessments.rationale: The last-admin invariant spans concurrent role and account-state changes under a shared lock.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 06/12] Signal tenant deactivation and drop the tenant's sockets, mail live sync and Semp entry
assessments.rationale: Transactional deactivation signals require three idempotent consumers and bounded shutdown.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 07/12] Export a tenant's data through an authenticated, expiring download
assessments.rationale: Tenant exports cross data, blobs, archive jobs, expiring authenticated downloads and cleanup.

assessments.title: [mt-realtime 04/04] Require a same-origin Origin on the WebSocket upgrade and on unsafe HTTP methods
assessments.rationale: One explicit Origin rule applies to two inbound paths with a precise rejection matrix.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 06/08] Restrict delegation targets to projects in the run's tenant
assessments.rationale: One authorization lookup extends the existing delegation contract and preserves pending-key cleanup.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 07/08] Bind project agent guidance ownership to the tenant's user
assessments.rationale: Defined owner guards extend existing reference and transaction boundaries without a new protocol.

assessments.title: [mt-agents 08/08] Cap concurrently running agent runs per tenant
assessments.rationale: An existing queue-lane pattern covers specified enqueue sites while preserving job keys.

assessments.title: [mt-ai-budgets 03/04] Report a user's own AI usage against their own caps
assessments.rationale: One usage report moves onto the established tenant budget store in two defined areas.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 08/12] Let a user or an admin delete an account
assessments.rationale: Irreversible account deletion combines self/admin authorization, concurrency and last-admin protection.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 09/12] Cancel a deactivated tenant's running agent runs in the agents process
assessments.rationale: A cancellation lifecycle spans in-flight registries, active model turns and agents-process shutdown.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 01/12] Refuse to start a service under a superuser, BYPASSRLS or table-owner database role
assessments.rationale: A precise assertion enforces the accepted runtime database-role contract at four service startups.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 10/12] Narrow /api/system-health to the caller's tenant
assessments.rationale: A bounded health-report rewrite uses tenant snapshots, existing SQL and two-tenant fixtures.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 02/12] Prove REST and MCP isolation with an exhaustive two-tenant route suite
assessments.rationale: An exhaustive REST/MCP security matrix needs representative fixtures and proof that no tenant data leaks.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 03/12] Prove realtime isolation with an exhaustive two-tenant frame suite
assessments.rationale: An exhaustive realtime security matrix needs deterministic absence-of-message assertions without sleeps.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 11/12] Purge a deleting tenant in chunks and record a tombstone
assessments.rationale: Chunked deletion combines foreign-key ordering, filesystem cleanup and tombstones with high error impact.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 04/12] Prove background isolation with an exhaustive two-tenant task suite
assessments.rationale: An exhaustive background-task matrix covers registries, queue affinity and tenant fingerprints across three services.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 05/12] Prove AI gateway isolation with an exhaustive two-tenant endpoint suite
assessments.rationale: Four defined AI gateway endpoints use the established tenant harness in a bounded test matrix.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 06/12] Release checkpoint — run a context-complete release cleanly in production for seven days
assessments.rationale: This issue requires manual operator or provisioning work and is not an agent implementation task.

assessments.title: [mt-ai-budgets 04/04] Remove the budget properties from the settings item (contract)
assessments.rationale: Specified obsolete budget properties and readers are removed after validating the contract prerequisites.

assessments.title: [mt-secrets 03/06] Seal new credentials under the tenant key
assessments.rationale: Credential encryption changes the stored cryptographic scheme and has high impact even with few touched files.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 07/12] Stamp the sole tenant onto legacy queued jobs and reject tenant tasks without a tenant
assessments.rationale: A precisely scoped legacy job-envelope backfill and existing registerTask guard enforce tenant stamps.

assessments.title: [mt-secrets 04/06] Re-encrypt existing credentials under their tenant key
assessments.rationale: Concurrency-safe credential re-encryption combines tenant keys, plaintext cleanup and resumable backfill.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 08/12] Drop the legacy global unique keys and the dormant resource_grants table (contract)
assessments.rationale: A destructive contract migration removes multiple global unique keys and requires exhaustive arbiter verification.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 09/12] Add tenant-consistent composite foreign keys between tenant tables
assessments.rationale: Tenant-consistent composite foreign keys span tables and partitions, two migrations and catalog verification.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 10/12] Switch to strict tenant enforcement in the database and in every process
assessments.rationale: Strict tenant enforcement changes database policies, runtime defaults and test fixtures across the application.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 11/12] Release checkpoint — run the strict release cleanly in production before the contract steps that need it
assessments.rationale: This issue requires manual operator or provisioning work and is not an agent implementation task.

assessments.title: [mt-secrets 06/06] Retire the master-key-only credential scheme (contract)
assessments.rationale: Retiring the legacy credential scheme changes public crypto interfaces after a verified backfill.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 05/10] Spawn stdio MCP servers through a sandbox launcher under a dedicated uid
assessments.rationale: A host sandbox launcher combines dedicated UID, socket transport, systemd and nftables in one lifecycle.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 06/10] Harden the service units with systemd sandboxing directives
assessments.rationale: Precisely specified systemd directives and writable paths extend existing units with a concrete validation matrix.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 07/10] Mark every API response uncacheable
assessments.rationale: One response-header invariant covers all HTTP branches with integration assertions.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 08/10] Throttle login, password reset and invitation acceptance per client IP
assessments.rationale: Auth throttling introduces bounded state, proxy identity and timing rules for several authentication paths.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 09/10] Remove user content from log lines
assessments.rationale: A bounded logging-payload rewrite uses existing fixtures to prove sensitive content is absent.

assessments.title: [mt-web 02/08] Add the password-reset page with the token in the URL fragment
assessments.rationale: A defined password-reset route and form connect several existing frontend/backend boundaries.

assessments.title: [mt-ops 10/10] Route realtime logging through the shared logger and forbid console in backend production code
assessments.rationale: A broad mechanical rewrite adopts the existing shared logger, lint restriction and adjusted spy tests.

assessments.title: [mt-accounts 12/12] Re-apply recorded deletions after a backup restore
assessments.rationale: Deletion replay after restoring old backups introduces a durable ledger, replay CLI and operational lifecycle.

assessments.title: [mt-web 03/08] Expose the session role and add the admin accounts page
assessments.rationale: Admin UI and adapters follow established web conventions with several defined states.

assessments.title: [mt-web 04/08] Add the admin invitations panel
assessments.rationale: An invitations panel follows the existing admin adapter and UI pattern.

assessments.title: [mt-web 05/08] Add the admin AI budgets panel
assessments.rationale: An AI budget panel follows existing adapters and UI patterns with defined validation and loading states.

assessments.title: [mt-web 06/08] Add the admin health panel and make the System page per-user
assessments.rationale: A bounded component extraction and admin panel use the existing health-report contract.

assessments.title: [mt-web 07/08] Add the account page with export and deletion
assessments.rationale: Export/deletion UI uses established APIs with precisely defined confirmations and session behavior.

assessments.title: [mt-web 08/08] Let admins delete an account from the accounts panel
assessments.rationale: One destructive UI action uses the existing backend guard and a mandatory confirmation.

assessments.title: [mt-enforcement 12/12] Verify the tenancy invariants at every deploy before activating a release
assessments.rationale: Cross-cutting catalog introspection must reject a deployment before activating a release when tenant invariants fail.

assessments.title: [mt-go-live 01/03] Security gate sign-off — verify strict isolation in production and record an external review before go-live
assessments.rationale: This issue requires manual operator or provisioning work and is not an agent implementation task.

assessments.title: [mt-go-live 02/03] Accept invitations — drop the single-tenant guard, then create and provision the invited account
assessments.rationale: Invitation acceptance removes singleton guards and atomically provisions an account with rollback.

assessments.title: [mt-go-live 03/03] Add the invitation acceptance page
assessments.rationale: The invitation page follows the established secret-fragment route pattern and public invitation API.

assessments.title: [followups-1099] Review follow-ups from PRs #944 and #1095 — epic
assessments.rationale: An epic coordinates child issues and is not an implementation dispatch.

assessments.title: [followups-1099 01/02] Route the property type migration's item writes through the choke-point
assessments.rationale: Two defined SQL write variants move through the existing choke-point boundary while preserving their transaction.

assessments.title: [followups-1099 02/02] Remove the redundant mkdir from the tenant entity test
assessments.rationale: One redundant mkdir and import are removed from a single test, with no runtime behavior change.

assessments.title: [model-routing S1] Enforce issue model tier metadata throughout authoring
assessments.rationale: This change establishes a cross-process routing and execution contract with failure and concurrency paths.

assessments.title: [model-routing S2] Apply explicit model policies to Relay workflows
assessments.rationale: This change establishes a cross-process routing and execution contract with failure and concurrency paths.

assessments.title: [model-routing S3] Backfill model tiers with a reversible audited manifest
assessments.rationale: This change establishes a cross-process routing and execution contract with failure and concurrency paths.
